transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

They sent me. My lieutenant did. I was just... at the station. Moving the airway bags. I had to put them in a pattern. The pattern I knew was right. I was... repeating the dispatch numbers out loud. He told me to stop and step away, but I wouldn't. I couldn't. If I broke the sequence... the whole bay would go bad. I just couldn't stop. So they made me come here.

When you were arranging those bags in the pattern and repeating the numbers, did you know at the time that it might seem unusual or excessive to someone else, or did it feel completely necessary and right?
I wasn't really... thinking about how it looked to him. Or to anyone else. It just... it had to be done that way. I don't know.
Looking back now, do you think the pattern had to be done that exact way, or do you recognize that maybe it didn't really matter and your mind was just making you feel like it had to be perfect?
I... I don't know. It just felt like it had to be that way. I wasn't really thinking about if it mattered. It just did.

Before you started arranging those bags in the pattern, did you have a thought or worry in your mind that something bad would happen if you didn't do it exactly right? Or did the urge to arrange them just come up without a specific worry?
I didn't... I wasn't really thinking about a specific bad thing. It was just... I just had to do it. The urge was just there.

When you get the urge to arrange things in that pattern or repeat the numbers, does it feel like your own thought that you want to do, or does it feel like a thought or urge that's pushing into your mind against your will?
I don't... I haven't really thought about it like that. It's just... in my head. I don't know if it's mine or not. It's just there.
When you have to arrange things in that pattern or repeat the numbers, does it cause you distress or anxiety? And does it interfere with your ability to do your job or other things you need to do?

I guess... yeah, it messes things up. I can't... I don't work on the ambulance anymore. They put me on desk duty, doing notes and checking equipment, but... I couldn't really do that either, so they took me off the schedule. And I don't really... I don't see my friends much now. Or do stuff around the house. It's just... hard to get things done.
When you have the urge to arrange things in that pattern or repeat the numbers, do you ever try to resist it or push it away, or does it feel so right that you don't really want to stop it?
I don't really try to stop it. It just... happens. I don't know about it feeling right, it's just what I do.
When you're arranging the bags or repeating the numbers, do you wish you could stop doing it, or does it feel like something you want to keep doing?
I don't really... wish anything about it. I just do it. It's not about wanting to or not wanting to.

Before you feel the urge to arrange things in that pattern or repeat the numbers, do you ever have a thought or worry that pops into your head that you don't want to have? Like a thought that bothers you or that you wish would go away?
No. I don't really have thoughts like that. It's just... I just do it.
When you're not actively arranging things or repeating numbers, do you ever have thoughts or images pop into your head that feel unwanted or uncomfortable — things you didn't choose to think about?
Not really. Like I said... I don't get stuff like that. There's no pictures or whatever popping up. It's just... regular.
If you could snap your fingers and never have to arrange things in that pattern or repeat those numbers again, would you want to? Or would you be okay with doing it forever?
I don't know. It doesn't really matter to me. I guess... I'm fine just doing it. It doesn't bother me.
When you're arranging those bags or repeating the numbers, do you feel like it's something that goes against who you are, or does it feel like it's just part of how you naturally are?
I don't know. It's just... what I do. It's just part of it. I don't really think about it like that.
When you're arranging the bags in that pattern or repeating the numbers, does it feel good or satisfying while you're doing it? Like, do you get any kind of pleasure or relief from it?
No. It doesn't... I don't feel anything like that. It's not about feeling good or getting relief. I just do it. It doesn't feel like much of anything.

When your lieutenant told you to stop arranging the bags and step away, how did that make you feel? Were you frustrated or upset that he was trying to make you stop, or did part of you actually want to stop but felt like you couldn't?

I wasn't... I wasn't upset with him. I just... I couldn't stop. I couldn't step away. He didn't understand. If I broke the sequence... if I stopped moving the bags into the pattern and saying the dispatch numbers... the whole bay would go bad. I had to keep doing it. That's why they sent me here.

When you say the whole bay would go bad if you broke the sequence — do you actually believe that would happen, or do you know that probably wouldn't happen but the feeling that it might is still very strong?

I know it would happen. It's not... it's not just a feeling. I know what's real. 

Just like I know what they're doing at the station. The injury review people and... some of the supervisors. They've been watching me through the cameras there. They go in and change my triage notes... trying to make me look unsafe. They tell me it's just routine paperwork, but... I know they're doing it. I know what's actually happening.

When you say the supervisors are changing your triage notes and watching you through the cameras — is there any chance you could be wrong about that, or are you completely certain that's actually happening?

I'm not wrong. ... I'm completely certain. 

I wouldn't say it if I wasn't. They keep telling me it's just routine paperwork, but... it's not. The injury review people and the supervisors... they watch the station cameras. They change my triage notes to make me look unsafe. I know what I see.
